name: Low Latency Mode
description: Limits how many frames the CPU queues ahead of the GPU (formerly 'Maximum pre-rendered frames').
effects: On (1 frame) reduces input latency when the GPU is the bottleneck. Ultra additionally schedules frames just in time.
tradeoffs: Can slightly reduce average FPS or increase stutter in CPU-bound games. Games with NVIDIA Reflex ignore it — use Reflex in-game instead.

recommendations.why: Reflex is more effective and overrides this.

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

valueNames.1: On (1 frame) — Ultra also reads as 1

notes: Ultra uses an additional internal driver flag that the public NVAPI headers don't document, so On and Ultra both read as '1 frame'.

name: Vertical sync
description: Synchronises frame presentation to the display refresh to prevent tearing.
effects: On removes tearing; Fast Sync allows uncapped rendering without tearing (needs FPS well above refresh).
tradeoffs: Adds input latency when FPS reaches the refresh rate. With G-SYNC, use V-Sync On in NVCP + Off in-game + a frame cap ~3 FPS below refresh.

recommendations.value: On (with a frame cap below refresh)
recommendations.why: Tear-free with minimal latency inside the VRR range.

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Max Frame Rate
description: Driver-level frame-rate cap.
effects: Caps FPS to reduce power, heat, and fan noise; keeps G-SYNC active when capped below refresh.
tradeoffs: In-game limiters and Reflex usually have lower latency than the driver limiter.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Background Application Max Frame Rate
description: Caps FPS for games running in the background (alt-tabbed).
effects: Saves power and heat when a game is minimised.
tradeoffs: None for the foreground game.

recommendations.why: Prevents a background game from heating the PC.

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Not readable through a documented interface — open the vendor control panel

name: G-SYNC application mode
description: Which applications may use variable refresh (G-SYNC / G-SYNC Compatible).
effects: Fullscreen and windowed allows VRR in borderless games.
tradeoffs: Windowed mode can cause flicker or slowdowns in some desktop apps on certain monitors.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → Display → Set up G-SYNC (enable per display and choose fullscreen/windowed).
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)
notes: G-SYNC must also be enabled per monitor in 'Set up G-SYNC', which is not exposed through the DRS profile settings.

name: Monitor technology
description: Per-application override of variable refresh (G-SYNC vs fixed refresh).
effects: Forcing fixed refresh disables VRR for that application.
tradeoffs: Fixed refresh reintroduces tearing/stutter in games below refresh.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Power management mode
description: How aggressively the GPU drops clocks when lightly loaded.
effects: 'Prefer maximum performance' keeps clocks high, avoiding brief clock ramp-up stutters in some games.
tradeoffs: Higher idle power and heat; on multi-monitor desktops the GPU may never idle down. Laptops lose battery life.

recommendations.why: Clocks ramp up instantly under load anyway.

recommendations.value: Prefer maximum performance (that game's profile only)

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Texture filtering - Quality
description: Overall texture filtering quality/performance trade-off.
effects: Higher performance settings apply filtering optimisations.
tradeoffs: Performance gains are negligible on modern GPUs; High performance can cause shimmering.

recommendations.why: No meaningful FPS gain from lower settings.

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Anisotropic filtering
description: Sharpens textures viewed at angles.
effects: 16x looks noticeably sharper on floors/roads.
tradeoffs: Very small performance cost on modern GPUs.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Anisotropic filtering mode
description: Whether the driver overrides the game's anisotropic filtering.
effects: Override forces the level above.
tradeoffs: Can conflict with games that already use AF.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Texture filtering - Negative LOD bias
description: Allows or clamps negative level-of-detail bias.
effects: Clamp reduces shimmering when anisotropic filtering is forced.
tradeoffs: None significant.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Texture filtering - Trilinear optimization
description: Uses bilinear filtering where differences are invisible.
effects: Tiny performance gain.
tradeoffs: Ignored when Quality is High quality.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Texture filtering - Anisotropic sample optimization
description: Reduces anisotropic samples for performance.
effects: Tiny gain.
tradeoffs: Can cause shimmering.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Antialiasing - Mode
description: Whether the driver overrides or enhances in-game antialiasing.
effects: Driver AA only works in older DirectX 9/OpenGL titles.
tradeoffs: Overriding can break modern deferred-rendering games; use in-game AA/DLSS instead.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Antialiasing - FXAA
description: Post-process antialiasing applied by the driver.
effects: Smooths edges cheaply.
tradeoffs: Blurs text and UI; stacks with in-game AA.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Image Scaling (NVIDIA Image Scaling)
description: Driver-level upscaling and sharpening for games that lack DLSS.
effects: Render below native resolution and upscale for higher FPS.
tradeoffs: Softer image than DLSS; also changes desktop resolution list when enabled.

recommendations.useCase: Games without DLSS on lower-end GPUs

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D settings → Image Scaling, or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Shader Cache
description: Stores compiled shaders on disk so games don't recompile them each launch.
effects: Reduces stutter and load times after the first run.
tradeoffs: Corrupt caches can cause stutter/glitches — clear them after driver updates if problems appear.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Shader Cache Size
description: Maximum disk space for the shader cache.
effects: Larger caches avoid evicting shaders for big game libraries.
tradeoffs: Uses disk space.

recommendations.value: 10 GB or Unlimited on SSDs with free space

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)
notes: Shown as stored by the driver (megabytes). The cache folders can be cleared with the NVIDIA app guide's 'Clear cache' action.

name: Threaded optimization
description: Lets the OpenGL driver use multiple CPU threads.
effects: Can improve FPS in CPU-bound OpenGL games.
tradeoffs: Rarely causes instability in old OpenGL titles.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Triple buffering (OpenGL)
description: Third frame buffer for OpenGL games with V-Sync.
effects: Smoother FPS with V-Sync on in OpenGL.
tradeoffs: Adds a frame of latency; only affects OpenGL.

recommendations.value: Off unless using V-Sync in OpenGL games

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Ansel / Photo mode
description: NVIDIA's in-game photo mode.
effects: Enables photo mode in supported games.
tradeoffs: None while unused.
whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Preferred graphics processor (laptops)
description: On hybrid-graphics laptops, which GPU runs an application.
effects: High-performance NVIDIA processor runs games on the dedicated GPU.
tradeoffs: Higher power use.

recommendations.why: Ensures the dedicated GPU is used.

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → 3D Settings → Manage 3D settings (Global or Program Settings), or NVIDIA App → Graphics. Windows' own per-app setting (Settings → Display → Graphics) takes priority on recent Windows versions.
readability: Read from the driver (NVAPI DRS)

name: Output dynamic range and colour format
description: RGB Full vs Limited range, colour depth, and format per display.
effects: Full range shows true blacks on PC monitors; Limited range causes washed-out greys.
tradeoffs: TVs may expect Limited; mismatches crush blacks or wash them out.

recommendations.value: Use NVIDIA colour settings: RGB, Full, highest bit depth
Match the TV's black level setting

whereToChange: NVIDIA Control Panel → Display → Change resolution → Use NVIDIA colour settings.
readability: Not readable through a documented interface — open the vendor control panel
